title: Without the Jargon: How It Decides To Act
markdown:
Every time Open Executive could take an action, it picks one of three modes. The mode depends on how routine and reversible the work is — not on guesswork.

| Mode | When | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Act on its own** | Routine, recoverable work — morning hygiene, meeting nudges, doc sweeps | It just does it and shows you what it did. No approval. |
| **Propose for approval** | Decisions that need a human signature — a new vendor, a hire, a customer-facing release | It drafts the work, parks it in the right person's queue, and sends nothing until they approve. |
| **Escalate to a human** | Sensitive or time-critical work — legal, a board-level event, an upset key customer | It puts the drafted response in front of the right person straight away, flagged urgent, even outside their working hours — and sends nothing until they approve. |

If you use Open Executive just for yourself (solo mode), there is nobody else to route to: every proposal comes to you, and you choose whether it books meetings on its own or asks you first.

Who approves a proposal is decided by **what someone is cleared to approve, not their job title.** Each person carries tags — "approve money under $10k," "sign off on hires," "onboard a new vendor." When a proposal needs sign-off, Open Executive routes it to whoever holds the matching tag. If nobody matches, it falls back to you. You are always the final stop.

*See also: Authority & Org for the implementation.*
